verdict.rationale: cubic's docs say every PR is scanned for logic errors and potential security vulnerabilities, and that it comments on bugs. Ultrareview adds a deeper multi-pass analysis, Datadog logs can confirm findings, and thumbs up/down feedback helps it separate useful findings from noise. However, race conditions and broken edge cases are never named, the docs also list style inconsistencies among its findings, and there is no independent evidence of real-bug catch rates. One non-expert user only says it gives more technical explanations than basic checks. missing for 10: documented detection of race conditions/concurrency bugs, documented edge-case detection, independent or hands-on evidence that it catches real bugs rather than nits, and precision or signal-to-noise data.

support.subject: As a developer, the reviewer catches real bugs in my PR — logic errors, race conditions, broken edge cases — not just style nits

citations.quote: The AI automatically scans every pull request for a wide range of issues, including logic errors, style inconsistencies, and potential security vulnerabilities.
Spots bugs and improvements: Comments on bugs and improvements in pull requests
It runs a longer, multi-pass analysis using cubic's most capable review models
Now you can connect Datadog, and cubic agents will check whether your production logs confirm their findings.
Thumbs up/down help cubic calibrate what's useful vs noise for your specific codebase
